appearance_facts.fact: Title text reads 'Incidence of Condition A in US States'.
Vertical color bar labeled 'High' at the top and 'Low' at the bottom, with tick values 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. The scale runs from dark red (low) through orange to pale yellow (high).
Large state polygon in the south-central region, labeled 'TX', filled with pale yellow color.
State polygon in the northwestern corner, labeled 'WA', filled with dark red color.
State polygon in the western region, located east of Utah and west of Kansas, filled with light gray color.
Minnesota (MN), Nebraska (NE), Oklahoma (OK), Georgia (GA), Florida (FL), and New York (NY) are also filled with dark red color.

Montana (MT), North Dakota (ND), South Dakota (SD), Wyoming (WY), Utah (UT), Illinois (IL), West Virginia (WV), Virginia (VA), South Carolina (SC), and Massachusetts (MA) are filled with pale yellow color.
California, Arizona, New Mexico (partially), Arkansas, Alabama, and Rhode Island are filled with light gray, distinct from the color scale.

printed_facts.fact: Y-axis ticks: 0 (bottom, 'Low'), 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 (top, 'High'). Color gradient: Dark Red -> Orange -> Pale Yellow.
TX is labeled in the large southern state. WA is labeled in the northwest state. CO is the unlabeled gray state in the western interior (between UT and KS).
Pale yellow corresponds to the top of the scale (approx 80-100). Dark red corresponds to the bottom of the scale (approx 0-20). Light gray is outside the scale range.
